text: I added a short article on how Aurangzeb won the war of succession, next to the lineage. It ends with what is still debated.

block.title: How Aurangzeb won the war of succession
block.because: You asked to go deeper on the succession

sections.md: In 1657 [[Shah Jahan|person]] fell ill, and all four of his sons moved to claim the throne [E]. [[Aurangzeb|person]] allied with [[Murad Bakhsh|person]], defeated [[Dara Shikoh|person]] at [[Samugarh|event]] in 1658 [E], and confined Shah Jahan in Agra Fort until his death in 1666 [E].

Aurangzeb had years of command experience in the Deccan and was skilled at winning over nobles [L]. Dara, the favoured heir at court, had less field experience [L]. Aurangzeb later had Murad executed and drove Shah Shuja into exile in Arakan, where he disappeared [E].

Later writers often cast the contest as a tolerant mystic (Dara) against an orthodox zealot (Aurangzeb); how far religion actually decided the outcome, rather than military and political skill, is debated [C].
